ECON 5351.title: Environmental Economics
ECON 5351.description: This course is an introduction to an economics perspective of environmental problems, with attention to public policy solutions to pollution and climate change challenges. Part I will cover the ways in which markets fail to efficiently allocate resources in the presence of pollution along with the class of Pigouvian policies used to correct those failures. Part II will focus on the empirical techniques used by economists to assess the cost and benefits of environmental policies.
cilos: Apply economic analysis to the management of the environment and natural resources.
Appreciate theoretical and empirical research in environmental economics.
Use economic principles and non-market valuation techniques to address a variety of continuing and contemporary environmental issues.
Explain the method in policy evaluation and develop policy evaluation report(s).
Demonstrate effective writing and communication skills in report preparation and presentation.

ECON 5352.title: Housing Economics
ECON 5352.description: Housing has its unique characteristics in terms of heterogeneity, durability, and spatial fixity. This suggests that the microeconomic implications for housing are different from those for a standard commodity. Besides, the macroeconomic implications of housing market fluctuations can be significant to the aggregate economy, given that many households borrow mortgages to finance their home purchases. This course addresses both the microeconomic and macroeconomic issues of housing. Topics include demand-supply and equilibrium analysis of housing, rationales and effects of certain public policies on housing, causes and consequences of housing market fluctuations, and housing market spillovers.
cilos: Apply the microeconomic concepts and models to conduct supply and demand analysis of housing markets.
Explain the economic rationales and effects of public policies on housing.
Apply the macroeconomic concepts and models to analyze the dynamics and spillovers of the housing market.
Use the relevant quantitative tools to carry out the empirical analysis of housing markets.
Formulate and conduct a secondary research project related to housing market issues.
Communicate the topic effectively in oral and written English.

ECON 5352.title: Housing Economics
ECON 5352.description: Housing has its unique characteristics in terms of heterogeneity, durability, spatial fixity, and high purchase price. This suggests that conventional economic concepts need to be readdressed in order to analyze housing. Besides, many households use mortgage loan to finance home purchase. A substantial collapse in house price might lead to negative equity for leveraged households and reduce their consumption and investment thereafter. This course studies both the microeconomic and macroeconomic issues of housing. Topics include housing demand and supply analysis, equilibrium models of housing market, rationales and effects of public policies on housing, causes and consequences of housing market dynamics and crisis. Applications to the subprime mortgage crisis and housing markets in Hong Kong and China will also be addressed.
cilos: Apply the microeconomic concepts and models to conduct supply and demand analysis of housing markets.
Explain the economic rationales and effects of public policies on housing.
Apply the macroeconomic concepts and models to analyze the dynamics and spillovers of the housing market.
Use the relevant quantitative tools to carry out the empirical analysis of housing markets.

Communicate the topic effectively in oral and written English.

ECON 5353.title: Value Investing in Global Markets
ECON 5353.description: This course covers the philosophy, theory, and practice of value investing as it has developed since Graham. Techniques of investing will be presented, including search, valuation, and portfolio construction. The focus will be on the economic analysis and valuation of firms, with the underlying goal of achieving a comprehensive understanding of each firm. The course will begin with an exploration of industry and market trends, followed by a systematic development of valuation techniques from the ground up, along with an examination of the limitations of current standard valuation methods. These techniques and the developed framework will be applied to study specific companies. Finally, the course will address portfolio construction and issues related to portfolio management.
cilos: Explain the methodology and philosophy of value investing, including key assumptions used, how value investing differs from other styles of investing and the strengths and limitations of this analysis framework.

Describe the key concepts, tools and frameworks of value investing, such as search, and different types of valuation, and how these types of valuation differ from each other and from those used elsewhere.
Apply economic tools and principles to identify and analyze actual real-world companies.
Communicate these findings to multiple stakeholders.

ECON 5360.title: Monetary Economics
ECON 5360.description: This course studies the basic theories of money and their applications to monetary issues. It also examines a class of phenomena related to banking, credits and liquidity from monetary perspective.

Learn the models implications to various monetary policy issues.
Learn analyzing dynamic models.

ECON 5370.title: Using Data for Economics Analysis
ECON 5370.description: This course puts econometrics theories and models into practice. Students are required to write their own program with R, and do a term project. ECON 5390.title: Labor Economics
ECON 5390.description: This course presents a theoretical and empirical analysis of labor markets, utilizing primarily the tools developed in microeconomics and econometrics. We will investigate how wages are determined in the labor market and study the effects of private and public policies on wages and employment. Issues about unemployment, taxation, minimum wage, and monopsony will be studied.
cilos: Identify economic critical thinking.
Utilize labor economics to explain pertinent economic and social phenomena.
Carry out independently applied research in economic and social problems of the labor market.
Apply economic theory to practical human resources situations and make sound economic decisions.

ECON 5390.title: Labor Economics
ECON 5390.description: This course presents a theoretical and empirical analysis of labor markets, utilizing primarily the tools developed in microeconomics and econometrics. We will investigate how wages are determined in various labor markets and study the effects of private and public policies on wages and unemployment. Issues about human capital and labor market discrimination will be studied. We will also examine how employers can design compensation packages, incentive contracts, and performance evaluations for their employees.

ECON 5410.title: Value Investing from an Economic Perspective
ECON 5410.description: This course will introduce the precepts of value investing.  It will focus on the equity market, and begin with the classic Graham and Dodd investing criteria.  This includes stock search; valuation; and design of optimal portfolio.  Innovations to the classic criteria as well as use of derivates in the portfolio will be introduced.
cilos: Describe the philosophy, style and tools of value investing.
Apply concepts in Accounting, Microeconomics and Corporate Finance to analyze companies and their stocks.
Write a research report.

ECON 5420.title: Topics in Development Economics
ECON 5420.description: The course investigates how economics grow, the meaning of "development", and the barriers individuals and countries face in achieving development. Topics include the poverty trap; how population growth affects economic growth; the rationale for government intervention in peoples' fertility choices; rural-to-urban migration and its socioeconomic implications; how credit market frictions affect economic activity and whether they can lead to poverty traps; how microcredit works and whether it helps to alleviate poverty; and the role of the state in economic development.
cilos: State and explain the theoretical and empirically observed relationship between economic growth and poverty reduction.
Analyze the theoretical mechanisms through which poverty might become a "trap".

Describe theoretical assumptions under which population growth might affect economic growth, provide economic explanations for fertility choices, describe the empirically observed relationship between economic growth and population growth and interpret it.
Describe credit market imperfections and analyze how market imperfections may impede growth, and in particular lead to a poverty trap.
Analyze the mechanisms that cause microcredit programmes to have high repayment rates, and provide possible explanations why they do not appear to lead to poverty reduction.

ECON 5510.title: International Trade
ECON 5510.description: International trade has become more and more important, as transportation costs and artificial trade barriers keep falling over time. The world is more and more integrated through trade. Trade also plays a very important role in the development of many emerging economies, such as China. This course discusses the determinants of the pattern of international trade, why nations trade, what they trade, the gains from trade, and the distributional effects of trade. Then, we go on to analyze the motives, consequence and welfare implications of trade policies, and political economy of trade, such as free trade agreements, and the World Trade Organization.
cilos: Understand the theories behind gains from trade, comparative advantage and trade, economies of scale and trade, distributional effects of trade, and trade policy, and in some cases, understand how to take the theory to the data and estimate the model empirically.

Apply the theories to analyze gains from trade, what determines comparative advantage, how comparative advantage determines trade pattern, how increasing returns to scale determines trade pattern, how trade affects factor returns and the effects of trade policy.

ECON 5560.title: Advanced International Trade and Investment
ECON 5560.description: This is an advanced course on the economics of international trade and foreign direct investment (FDI). In this course, students learn to analyze the causes and consequences of international trade and foreign direct investment. Topics include the sources of gains from trade, the determinants of trade pattern, offshoring, multinational production, geography & trade, and implications of trade policies.
cilos: Know the different theories that seek to explain the causes of trade, gains from trade and pattern of trade flow.
Analyze the impact of trade on individual economies and to the world, including the aspects of welfare, growth and resource allocation.
Analyze the causes and consequences of trade protection.
Explain the gap between the theory and observed facts about international trade.
Know the economics of the world trading system.

ECON 5580.title: International Economics
ECON 5580.description: The course aims to familiarize graduate students with theories of international macroeconomics and related research questions. It focuses on determination of the current account and exchange rate, business cycle co-movement, and optimal monetary policy in open economies.
cilos: Have an up-to-date and in-depth knowledge on international macroeconomics. Understand the important questions in the literature and the main components of international macroeconomic theories.
Grasp the advanced mathematical and quantitative tools to understand the important research questions discussed in the literature.

Apply the concepts, principles, and models learnt in this course to analyze economic phenomena, understand and evaluate the international macroeconomics policies, possible effects and causes of
recent financial crisis, and financial and monetary policies that may stabilize fluctuations.
Develop new research questions independently based on the literatures and current macroeconomic phenomenon; and carry out research independently to address these questions.
Think critically and creatively when making effective economic decisions and policy suggestions supported by international macroeconomic theories and analytical and quantitative techniques.
Communicate effectively in oral and written English.
Demonstrate proficiency in using mathematical, quantitative and empirical tools to conduct economics research.
Locate, gather, and analyze data using appropriate information technology, software and systems.

ECON 5610.title: Cheap-Talk: Theory and Experiment
ECON 5610.description: This course covers game-theoretic works on communication. It maintains a healthy balance between classic/core papers and more recent papers, and between theory papers and experimental papers. Some of the topics covered is sender-receiver games, mediated communication, psychological aspects of communication, and game theory at the intersection of economics and linguistics. The goal is to stimulate original (theoretical and/or experimental) research in one of these areas.
cilos: Explain the theoretical and experimental concepts of game theory.
Describe, analyze and summarize data sets.
Carry out original research in related areas.
Develop original paper and proposal for theory and experimental ideas respectively.
Conclude precisely the ideas presented.

ECON 5611.title: Advanced Topics in Behavioral Decision Theory
ECON 5611.description: Behavioral economics stresses the need to incorporate psychological considerations into economics. The course covers decision making under risk, across time and involving others. Students will develop research skills on how to incorporate psychology to explain economic behavior, and how to apply behavioral economics to various economic and business settings.
cilos: Know the limitation of classic economic models and avoid wrong assumptions and conclusions.
Understand the underlying psychology of human behavior and apply in decision making.
Understand behavioral theory that extends classic economic models to capture psychology and apply to real situation.
Propose experiments to test theories.
Propose psychological underpinnings underlying choice behavior.
Develop research ideas on behavioral economics.

ECON 5620.title: Theory of Industrial Organization
ECON 5620.description: This course surveys recent advances in the theory of industrial organization, with the objective of preparing students to develop their own research ideas in related areas. Relevant tools of dynamic game theory, mechanism and information design are introduced. Topics such as competition and pricing, contract design and information disclosure will be covered.
cilos: Use industrial organization concepts or theories acquired through this course to explain and analyze real-life economic issues.
Form informed opinion on the contributions of a research paper and propose potential follow-up research projects.
Develop simple theoretical models to conduct industrial organization research.

ECON 5630.title: Empirical Industrial Organization
ECON 5630.description: This course covers various econometric methods used in industrial organization that is often referred to as the structural estimation approach. These methods have been gradually developed since 1980s in parallel with the modernization of industrial organization based on the game theory and now widely applied in antitrust policy, business strategy, and neighboring fields such as labor economics and international economics. This course presumes a good understanding of PhD-level microeconomics and microeconometrics. Participants are expected to understand at least UG-level industrial organization. This course requires participants to write programs mostly in R and sometimes in C++ to implement various econometric methods.
cilos: Explain the theory behind the econometric methods for industrial economics.
Implement the methods by writing programs using R and C++.
Critically assess the question, motivation, method, materials, and implications of research papers.
Discuss the contemporary business and organizational issues as analyzed in recent industrial economics papers.

ECON 5640.title: Policy Evaluation and Evidence Based Policy Making
ECON 5640.description: This course has two objectives: 1) to provide basic tools and skills for evaluating public policies in both developed and developing countries, and 2) to learn, through examples, how these tools and skills are actually applied to public policy evaluation. The case studies will focus on human capital development such as health, education, and labor policies.
cilos: Develop cognitive skill: Evaluate and compare differing social scientific perspectives on public policy evaluation and design.
Evaluate current public health, education, and labor policies: Critically assess existing public policies and develop empirical tools to evaluate their impacts.
Apply evaluation skills to policies: Perform data analysis using Excel and Stata.
Create professional writing skills: Write reaction papers for an academic audience.
Develop interpersonal skills: Present, discuss, evaluate and defend supplemental readings in front of a large group.

ECON 5650.title: The Asset Management Industry
ECON 5650.description: This course will examine the global asset management industry, focusing on the innovations and challenges that have been driving developments in the industry since the 2008 Financial Crisis.
cilos: Explain the macro-economic environment and its implications for the industry.
Gain an understanding on passive vs active investing including what both mean, the threat that passive investing poses to active managers, and asset managers’ response so far to the threat.
Explain what behavioural economics can tell about observed behaviours in the asset management industry.
Gain an understanding of what Private Markets are, their performance and implications for the broader economy.
Gain an understanding on what Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) investing is, and its impact so far on the asset management industry.

ECON 5660.title: The Economics of ESG Investing
ECON 5660.description: This course will examine topics in investing according to Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) principles, a major phenomenon in the global investment industry.
cilos: Explain the welfare implications of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) issues using economic theories.
Explain steps taken by companies to address ESG issues and the implications on their financial performances.
Gain an understanding on the role of ESG data and index providers and the importance of the information to asset managers.
Integrate ESG issues to the investment process from the asset managers’ perspective.

ECON 5670.title: Urban Economics
ECON 5670.description: This course discusses the economics of cities in the context of housing, labor, and transportation. Topics include business and individual location decisions, land use, urban amenities, agglomeration economies, local governance, etc. The course covers empirical methods for urban policy analysis, such as the hedonic model, and discrete choice models. This course also discusses advanced general equilibrium models used in contemporary urban literature, including quantitative spatial models. Students will learn basic tools for the visualization of spatial GIS data, and analytical tools for empirical evaluations of urban policies.
cilos: Understand the key concepts, principles, and models of urban economics.
Collaborate and communicate effectively in oral and written English on issues regarding urban economics.
Analyze the consequence of an urban policy and provide policy suggestions to governments and international organizations.
Develop an academic or career interest in urban economics.

This course also discusses advanced general equilibrium models used in contemporary urban literature, including household sorting models, and quantitative spatial models. Students will learn basic tools for the visualization of spatial GIS data, and analytical tools for empirical evaluations of urban policies.

ECON 5700.title: Macroeconomic and Financial Risk Management
ECON 5700.description: Financial institutions encounter different kinds of risks resulting from changes in macroeconomic or financial conditions. These include changes in interest rates, equity or commodity prices, exchange rates, corporate or sovereign credit rating, government policy or regulation, and political stability. Those changes may affect their economic profit or investment return. This course introduces fundamental concepts and methods of risk management. It focuses on the identification, quantification, and management of various economic and financial risks. Problems and challenges that arise in the risk management process are also addressed.
cilos: Analyze qualitatively and quantitatively economic and financial risk exposures for financial institutions.
Apply risk management tools and procedures to manage economic and financial risks.
Address problems and challenges in the risk management process.

ECON 5700.title: Macroeconomic and Financial Risk Management
ECON 5700.description: Macroeconomic and financial risk is the likelihood that changes in macroeconomic or financial conditions like interest rates, exchange rates, sovereign credit rating, government policy or regulation, political stability, commodity prices, or equity prices will affect the economic profit or investment return of an entity. This course introduces fundamental concepts of macroeconomic and financial risk management. It focuses on the identification, quantification, and management of various macroeconomic and financial risks. It evaluates and applies different tools and procedures, comprising quantitative measures and qualitative assessment, to measure and manage risk. Problems and challenges that arise in risk management process are also addressed.
cilos: Analyze qualitatively and quantitatively economic and financial risk exposures for financial institutions.

ECON 6520.title: Seminar in Economic Design
ECON 6520.description: In this course we deep-dive into market design, that is, the application of economic theory to designing or improving various kinds of market mechanisms. In particular, we will focus on two kinds of market mechanisms: matching and auction. If time permits, we may also discuss the design of financial markets. We will learn some theory, and then we will also learn how to use the theory to analyze and design markets for practical use. This course will be taught in a seminar format. Prepare to actively participate in discussions.
cilos: Read, analyze, and critique papers in the area of economic design.
Survey literature and know how to dissect and effectively digest a sizable body of papers.
Deliver technical presentation and know how to structure motivation, modeling, and analysis in a talk.
Develop and operationalize a research idea and put ideas into a presentable research proposal.

ECON 6900.title: Economics Practicum
ECON 6900.description: This course provides MSc in Economics students with a unique opportunity to bridge theory and practice by engaging in real-world applications of their academic training. The Practicum enables students to cultivate professional competencies, gain meaningful exposure to applied economic work, and develop a richer appreciation of the challenges and complexities encountered in the field.
